extracted.intended_audience: Authors of randomized trial reports, journal editors, peer reviewers, trialists, guideline developers, and other users of trial reports (including patients and the public)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing and evaluating primary reports of randomized controlled trials, providing a 30-item minimum checklist and flow diagram to ensure clear, complete, and transparent reporting from protocol to publication. Intended to be used by authors when preparing manuscripts and by editors and reviewers when assessing completeness of reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT 2025 30-item checklist (minimum reporting set)
rubrics_metrics.description: The CONSORT 2025 statement comprises a 30-item checklist of essential items that should be included when reporting the results of a randomized trial and a diagram for documenting the flow of participants through the trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use CONSORT 2025 as the minimum set of items to include in a trial report; it supersedes CONSORT 2010. The checklist focuses on the most common two-group parallel design but provides guidance for all randomized trials. The statement should be used alongside the CONSORT 2025 explanation and elaboration document which provides rationale, examples of good reporting, and empirical evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flow diagram of participant progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a diagram documenting the flow of participants through the phases of a randomized trial (enrolment, intervention allocation, follow-up and data analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a CONSORT-style flow diagram detailing numbers at each stage; helps readers assess participant flow and attrition. The flow diagram is a required complement to the checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open science section (structure and items)
rubrics_metrics.description: A new section in the checklist on open science that groups conceptually linked items such as trial registration (item 2), where the trial protocol and statistical analysis plan can be accessed (item 3), sharing of de-identified participant level data (item 4), and funding and conflicts of interest (item 5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restructure reports to make open science elements explicit. State registry details, where to access protocol and SAP, data sharing plans and mechanisms, and full funding/COI information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 4 — Data sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Report where and how individual de-identified participant data, statistical code, and any other materials can be accessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe whether and how de-identified participant-level data, analysis code, and supporting materials will be shared (including timing, repositories, access conditions). If sharing is planned but deferred (e.g., after an embargo), report those details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 5b — Financial and other conflicts of interest of manuscript authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Report financial and other conflicts of interest of the manuscript authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare funding sources and all relevant author-level conflicts using ICMJE or equivalent forms; include non-financial interests where relevant. Place information in the manuscript and upload completed disclosure forms as supplementary material if required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 8 — Patient and public involvement (PPI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report how patients and/or the public were involved in the design, conduct, and/or reporting of the trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the nature and extent of PPI (who was involved, what roles they played, how input influenced the trial) or explicitly state if no PPI occurred. Use this information to enhance transparency about stakeholder involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 12b — Eligibility criteria for sites and intervention deliverers
rubrics_metrics.description: Report eligibility criteria for sites and for individuals delivering the interventions, where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe site-selection criteria and any eligibility or training/qualification requirements for those delivering the interventions to allow assessment of intervention fidelity and generalizability of delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 15 — Assessment of harms and unintended effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Report how harms and other unintended effects were assessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide methods for harm collection, definitions used, timing, and analytic approach. Integrates items from CONSORT Harms extension; detail measurement and analysis of adverse events and unintended consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Items 21b/21c — Analysis population definitions and missing data handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Define who is included in each analysis (for example, all randomized participants) and in which group (item 21b), and report how missing data were handled in the analysis (item 21c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state primary analysis population(s) (e.g., intent-to-treat, per-protocol), describe any deviations, and detail methods used to handle missing outcome or covariate data (imputation methods, sensitivity analyses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 24 — Intervention delivery and concomitant care (24a, 24b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report how the intervention and comparator were actually administered (item 24a) and details of concomitant care received during the trial (item 24b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide practical details on delivery (who delivered, setting, timing, dose, adherence) and any co-interventions or background care that participants received during the trial to allow replication and interpretation. Integrates TIDieR and non-pharmacologic extension elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 3 (revised) — Where to access protocol and statistical analysis plan (SAP)
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to the trial protocol, report where the statistical analysis plan can be accessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give URLs/DOIs or repository accession details for protocol and SAP; if not publicly available explain why and how they can be requested. This supports transparency and assessment of prespecification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 10 (revised) — Reporting of changes after trial commencement
rubrics_metrics.description: Report important changes to the trial after it commenced, including any outcomes or analyses that were not prespecified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe modifications to protocol, outcomes, eligibility, sample size, analyses and provide timing, rationale, and whether changes were documented in protocol amendments or registry updates. Distinguish prespecified from post hoc analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 26 (revised) — Participant numbers and available data for each outcome and time point
rubrics_metrics.description: For each primary and secondary outcome — report the number of participants included in the analysis and the number of participants with available data at each time point for each treatment group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present denominators and attrition for outcomes at each assessment point (e.g., N analyzed, N with data), enabling readers to assess missingness and robustness. Consider tables and flow diagrams to communicate this clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 30 — Trial limitations including generalizability
rubrics_metrics.description: Trial limitations should include discussion of generalizability (previously a separate item), now incorporated under trial limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss limitations related to internal and external validity, including applicability of findings to other settings, populations, and delivery contexts. Be explicit about sources of bias and uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of CONSORT extension items (harms, outcomes, non-pharmacologic, TIDieR, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrate checklist items from key CONSORT extensions that apply to many trials, including items on reporting how harms were assessed and analysed (items 7, 15, 21a, 23a, 27), how outcomes were measured and analysed (items 14, 26), and how intervention and comparator were administered and by whom (item 24).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where extension-specific items are relevant, use the relevant CONSORT extension(s) alongside CONSORT 2025. The update integrates and harmonizes many extension items into the main checklist where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expanded CONSORT 2025 checklist (critical elements, bullet points)
rubrics_metrics.description: An expanded version of the CONSORT 2025 checklist provides bullet points eliciting critical elements of each item (an abridged version of elements from the explanation and elaboration document).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the expanded checklist to ensure inclusion of essential subelements of each item; the expanded checklist omits examples/references and is intended to facilitate implementation (e.g., in author checklists, peer-review tools).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to submit completed CONSORT checklist with manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are strongly recommended to submit a completed CONSORT 2025 checklist as part of the manuscript submission process, detailing where in the manuscript checklist items are reported, and upload it as part of the supplementary materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals should request the completed checklist and update author instructions to refer to CONSORT 2025. Providing the completed checklist facilitates editorial and peer-review assessment of reporting completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT is a reporting guideline, not a quality assessment instrument
rubrics_metrics.description: CONSORT 2025 provides recommendations on what to report; it is not intended to be used as a tool for assessing the quality of trial design, conduct, or analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use CONSORT to improve transparency of reporting about aspects related to internal and external validity; do not conflate completeness of reporting with methodological quality, though transparent reporting can reveal methodological deficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage use of supplementary materials and data/code sharing for transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should use online supplementary material to allow more detailed reporting of trial methods and results than may be permissible in the main article, and should provide detailed information on whether full data and code sharing is happening or planned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide protocols, SAPs, full analysis code, and extended methods/results as supplementary files or in repositories; specify access conditions and any embargoes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment and explicit reporting between protocol, SAP, registry, and manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure alignment of the information reported in the trial protocol, statistical analysis plan, trial registry, and trial report; explicitly state what was done and acknowledge if something was not done or was modified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report prespecified outcomes and analyses, and transparently disclose any deviations with rationale and timing. Cross-reference registry and protocol entries and provide access links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmonisation with SPIRIT and use across trial lifecycle
rubrics_metrics.description: CONSORT 2025 has aligned wording with SPIRIT 2025 where appropriate to provide consistent guidance from the trial protocol (SPIRIT) to the trial report (CONSORT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SPIRIT for protocol reporting and CONSORT for trial reports; harmonised items facilitate consistent reporting across study documents and aid users in tracking prespecification and changes.
